profiles.field_rule: Research trial: fountain grass forms a basal tuft and a long pink or burgundy bristled foxtail-like head. The visible bristles surround fascicles; they are not lemma awns or fused sandbur involucres. Compare Cenchrus ciliaris and Setaria, and inspect leaf ligule hairs with a lens. Published photos are nonlocal examples; ornamental planting is not evidence of establishment or native status.

profiles.field_rule: Research trial: large bushy, often silver-pink plumed panicle above upright/arching leafy stems with a pale central midrib. It forms clumps and short rhizomes; use only visibly confirmed structures. Distinguish from pampas grass, switchgrass and Arundo by actual paired spikelets, long callus hairs and conspicuous midrib—not solely ornamental setting. Lemma awns are fine and not reliably apparent from general photos, so awns stay unscored.
